cases.evidence: Output used only 3 tags though sentence has multiple clauses/appositives; produced fragmented, duplicated pieces.
cases.proposed_rule: Enforce the format constraint: if a sentence contains >1 parenthetical/appositive or multiple locative phrases, emit at least 4 boundary tags so clauses and appositives can be separated.

example_pair.input: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.
example_pair.output: The native inhabitants of Greenland <SEG:2> call themselves Inuit in Canada <SEG:1> and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, <SEG:3> in Greenland.

cases.evidence: Emitted a predication after the temporal phrase 'in 1861' before the verb 'was opened' arrived, so the translation asserted the wrong event.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not emit a predication when only a temporal adjunct (e.g., 'in 1861', 'on Tuesday') has arrived; wait for the following verb or noun that names the event.

example_pair.input: Downhill skiing as a sport goes back to at least the 17th century, and in 1861 the first recreational ski club was opened by Norwegians in Australia.
example_pair.output: Downhill skiing as a sport goes back to at least the 17th century, <SEG:4> and in 1861 the first recreational ski club was opened by Norwegians in Australia. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Emitted 'only the head' before 'and shoulders' arrived, causing translation to claim exclusivity for head alone.
cases.proposed_rule: Delay emitting exclusive limiters (e.g., 'only', 'just') until coordinated items or conjunctions they may scope over have been observed.

example_pair.input: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.
example_pair.output: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin <SEG:4> will be disappointed <SEG:1> as only the head and shoulders are visible. <SEG:3>

cases.evidence: Fragment ended after opening a subordinate clause ('in which...') and the translator rendered it as a complete proposition, introducing incorrect meaning.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not render an opened subordinate clause (e.g., beginning with 'in which', 'where', 'that') as a standalone proposition; wait for its main verb or complement.

example_pair.input: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.
example_pair.output: The balance of power was a system <SEG:1> in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Translator emitted a full clause 'This will cause' and then later re-emitted an overlapping main clause, producing duplication/incoherence.
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid emitting a standalone main clause if the following fragment is a noun phrase or relative clause that should be attached; either attach the NP to the existing predicate or wait for following modifiers.

example_pair.input: The glaciers are not stable, but flow down the mountain. This will cause cracks, crevasses, which may be obscured by snow bridges.
example_pair.output: The glaciers are not stable, but flow down the mountain. <SEG:1> This will cause cracks and crevasses, which may be obscured by snow bridges. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Boundary occurred before the head noun 'most commonly spoken language' arrived, causing the translator to pick an incorrect head and render the phrase wrongly.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not produce or choose a head noun (or finalize noun phrase meaning) before the source head word appears; wait for the head before emitting dependent nouns/complements.

example_pair.input: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.
example_pair.output: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. <SEG:1> It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Boundary cut before the possessive/complement 'of your stay', so translator asserted that the ticket itself proves the length rather than that it is needed to prove it.
cases.proposed_rule: Don't attach a modifier or assign a function (e.g., 'proves the length') to a noun until its following complement/possessor ('of your stay') or verb has been observed; otherwise keep phrasing neutral.

example_pair.input: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.
example_pair.output: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. <SEG:1> A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Boundaries split before appositive labels ('called arteries/veins'), so the translator assigned 'arteries' to the wrong predicate and reversed roles.
cases.proposed_rule: Wait for naming/appositive phrases (e.g., 'called X', 'known as X') before assigning that label to a preceding or following role or verb.

example_pair.input: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.
example_pair.output: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. <SEG:1> The smallest tubes are called capillaries. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Translator committed polarity before the negating complement was complete, producing the opposite inference (claims people mostly search beforehand).
cases.proposed_rule: Delay finalising polarity for negating adverbials or prepositional negations (e.g., 'without', 'rarely') until their full complement or coordinated list has been observed.

example_pair.input: Nowadays air travel is only rarely booked directly through the airline without first searching and comparing prices.
example_pair.output: Nowadays air travel is only rarely booked directly through the airline without first searching and comparing prices. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Fragment ended while 'taking the' lacked its object; translation guessed or finalized the object incorrectly before 'iPhone' arrived.
cases.proposed_rule: Don't finalise a verb's object or role for 'taking the ...' constructions until the object noun has arrived.

example_pair.input: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the device by walking onto the stage and taking the iPhone out of his jeans pocket.
example_pair.output: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the device <SEG:1> by walking onto the stage and taking the iPhone out of his jeans pocket. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Fragment ended after 'they still' (aux/adverb) without the main verb, so the emitted predicate asserted continuity incorrectly.
cases.proposed_rule: If a fragment ends with an auxiliary/adverb like 'still' and the main verb hasn't arrived, wait for the verb before producing a predicate translation.

example_pair.input: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
example_pair.output: The original population hasn't changed at all, <SEG:1> they still need the same adaptations as before. <SEG:2>

cases.evidence: Segmentation splits inside a noun phrase with apposition ('called ziggurats'), producing awkward/incomplete pieces and lowering adequacy.
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid splitting inside complex noun phrases that include appositives or parenthetical names; wait for the appositive and the following verb to close the NP.

example_pair.input: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
example_pair.output: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Boundary before the contrast and verb caused confusion about scope of 'Only' and mis-linked subject/verb, harming adequacy.
cases.proposed_rule: When a sentence begins with a scope-limiting word (e.g., 'only', 'just') that contrasts with 'not X' constructions, wait for the contrasting items and the verb before finalising scope.

example_pair.input: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.
example_pair.output: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear, were conditional on regular weekly structured PA sessions. <SEG:1>

summary: Most failures are placement errors: the prompt allows boundaries inside open clauses, before head nouns, appositives or polarity complements, causing premature commitments (wrong head, scope or polarity). Fixes should make the model wait for disambiguating heads, appositives, coordinated items and verb/complement heads before emitting a predication or assigning labels; also enforce the output format minimum tag rule.
